I built the McCartney Index once already, comparing seven countries on the same tour. Then I realized I have my own version: four Paul McCartney shows, four different countries, four different tours, at whatever tier I actually bought.

Uruguay, 2014, standing floor: 3.5 days of local minimum wage. Mexico, 2023, standing floor: 5.7 days. Argentina, 2019, premium standing: 12.6 days. Brazil, 2024, premium standing: 21 days. Twenty one days of minimum wage for one night, in my own country.

This is not a clean experiment like the first index. Different tours, different years, different currencies moving at different speeds. Mexico's ticket here is regular standing, not premium, because that's what I actually bought that year. And I no longer have the receipts, so each number is the official box office price of my tier at the time, not a crumpled ticket stub. I am not pretending otherwise.

But that is also the point. The clean version tells you what the product costs. This one tells you what my own choices cost, premium standing almost every time, across a decade of chasing the same band around a continent, and there is a real gap in the middle: my personal ticket cost is a story of income too, not just of prices.

What's your version of this, the thing you keep paying for at wildly different relative costs?
